result_text:
The default scoping rule now treats any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` as mock-resources test code, at any depth and with backslash paths too. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes offline (332 tests, 0 failures, 3 skipped).

**Change**

- `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around lines 393–394): the two mock conventions now use `[^/]*` instead of `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`:
  - `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`
  - `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`

  The `[^/]*` form keeps the match inside one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` stay out. It also covers plain `mock/`, punctuation like `mock.data` or `mock(old)`, and non-ASCII names. Windows paths are already normalised by `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches`, so the backslash variant works without extra patterns. The existing `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` cases still match.

**Test added**

- `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsMockTest.java` checks the positive cases (the new folder kinds plus the existing ones, with both slash styles) and the negative ones (`remock`, `demo`, `src/main/java`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`). Both of its tests pass.

I did not commit anything.
